title.narrative: Somalia Enhancing Public Resource Management Project

description.narrative: The Somalia Enhancing Public Resource Management Project (SERP, P177298) was approved by the Board of Executive Directors on December 14, 2022, and became effective on October 30, 2023. As of March 31, 2026, the project has been effectively under implementation for about two and half years years. The Bank conducted a mid-term review (MTR) of the project in September 2025 and the MTR identified the need for additional financing and recommended for the project to be restructured with a closing date extension and revision to the project scope and results framework to achieve the PDO. The rationale for the additional financing (AF) and restructuring is to improve operational efficiency for the Federal Republic of Somalia and the Somali citizens, that will include; a) dropping activities that have not been initiated, are no longer realistic to meet their related results indicators and are non-critical to the PDO and results framework, b) prioritizing activities that have been initiated and that are critical to achieving results; c) funding priority activities which will require reallocating budget across components; d) revising results indicators/targets to align with what is feasible to be completed within the project timeline, including consideration for new indicators that better reflect contribution of key project investments; e) extending the closing date by one year from December 31, 2027, to December 31, 2028, to allow for completion of critical activities with additional financing and full achievement of the PDO; and f) amending the legal agreements and subsidiary agreements as necessary.The SERP, with the proposed additional financing and restructuring, remains highly relevant to the Federal Republic of Somalia's (FRS) development agenda and the World Bank Group's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for the FRS FY24-28. SERP is aligned with the FRS's National Transformation Plan (NTP) 2025-2029 core objective of establishing and strengthening institutions for transparent, accountable, and inclusive governance. Specifically, SERP contributes to NTP's transformational governance pillar. SERP also supports the strategic objectives of the Public Finance Management Reform Strategy (PFMRS) 2026-2030 and the Medium-Term Revenue Roadmap (MTRR) 2024-2027. With respect to the CPF, SERP is a key engagement instrument to achieve the two foundational high-level objectives of the CPF: (i) increasing the effectiveness, transparency, and accountability of institutions and (ii) strengthening macroeconomic and fiscal management. SERP also continues to support building country systems through the various professional training and certification activities in PFM, DRM and PSM, the enhancement of the financial management information systems and their roll-out to other jurisdictions, ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs), local governments and public enterprises, and the development and implementation of ITAS to modernize tax administration, among others.
To strengthen accountability, transparency and institutional capacity in public resource management, across participating entities
